maya: quick heads-up — noticed a throughput regression on streaming requests when continuous batching is enabled. p95 for short streams (<=4 tokens) climbed ~30-40% after yesterday's runtime rollout. traces point to more frequent early flushes + partial-decode preemption. anyone else seeing this? cc @liam @sasha

liam: yup, bumped into it during morning noise. ran nsys over a mixed workload for ~30m on canary. two signals: (1) batch formation rate dropped ~15% because more streams are being flushed before batch windows close, (2) kernel chooser is falling back to the small-kernel codepath for ~22% of batches — seems tied to short sequence lengths right after a partial decode.

liam: profiling snippet:```text
Batch stats (canary):
- avg batch size: 7.2 -> 5.8 (post-rollout)
- early_flush_count: 432 -> 1291
Kernel choices:
- large-kernel: 68%
- small-kernel: 22% (was ~9% before)
GPU stalls: spikes around partial-decode completions, nvtx shows frequent kernel handoffs.
```

sasha: did we change the token_budget target for streams? i vaguely remember a tweak to favor latency in the sticky PR. that would explain more early flushes.

maya: yep — token_budget for streaming clients was lowered from 256 -> 128 to reduce tail for longer responses. unintended side-effect: for many small interactive streams we now hit token budget early and flush small micro-batches.

rohit: adding KV cache angle: when partial decode triggers a flush mid-prefetch we cancel ongoing KV warmups. that causes repeated prefetchs and cudaMemcpy churn. spotted a clear pattern: prefetch start -> flush -> prefetch cancel -> redo => jitter. logs:```text
[kv] prefetch start id=0x3f9 ts=170xxxxxxx
[kv] flush request stream_id=abc ts=170xxxxxxx+12ms
[kv] prefetch cancel id=0x3f9 reason=flush
[kv] prefetch restart id=0x4b2
```

perf-bot: alert: p95_stream_latency increased 34% (canary) — top correlated features: early_flush_count, small-kernel-percentage, kv-prefetch-cancel-rate.

dev-bot: quick idea: implement a "drip-window" soft-hold for streaming inputs: hold an incoming stream for up to X ms (e.g., 6-10ms) or until token_budget hits threshold, whichever comes first. this should coalesce many 1-2 token streams into larger batches while preserving tail latency for clients that truly need immediate streaming. tradeoffs: slightly higher median latency for some streams, but much better GPU efficiency and fewer kernel fallback events.

liam: concrete experiment proposal:
1) Canary A: revert token_budget for streaming back to 192 (middle ground)
2) Canary B: keep token_budget=128 + enable drip-window 8ms soft-hold
3) Kernel tweak: bias kernel selector to prefer large-kernel if estimated post-decode seq_len + prefetch_lag > 12 tokens (avoid fallback thrash)
4) KV change: add graceful prefetch completion window — don't cancel a prefetch if a flush happens within 5ms of prefetch completion (to avoid thrash)

sasha: i'll add instrumentation for: early_flush_reason (token_budget|timeout|client-eof), per-stream prefetch state transitions, kernel-choice-epoch tagging. need those metrics to evaluate A/B.

rohit: i'll run synthetic microbursts (1-3 token streams at 500rps) against both canaries and collect nvprof/nsys traces. will also add a counter for prefetch-cancels per-second.

maya: sounds good. if Canary A (revert token_budget) reduces p95 by >20% w/o hurting long-response tails, we can ship that as immediate rollback. Canary B is lower-risk longer-term tune (drip-window + kernel bias).

liam: one more perf detail — partial-decode scheduler currently preempts kernel handoffs aggressively to favor low-latency completions. that helps single-stream latency but increases fragmentation across the batcher. we should consider a fairness knob: allow a short non-preempt window (e.g., 4ms) where partial-decode completion waits to let the batcher finish handoffs if more inflight requests are about to join.

sasha: i'll add those two knobs to the runtime config: `stream_token_budget`, `drip_window_ms`, `partial_decode_nonpreempt_ms`, `kernel_bias_threshold`. will instrument via tracepoints.

maya: action items:
- liam: run canary A/B and post p50/p95/p99 + batch histograms (ETA 4h)
- sasha: add tracepoints & dashboard tiles for early_flush_reason + prefetch-cancels (ETA 2h)
- rohit: synthetic microburst traces + nsys dumps (ETA 3h)
- maya: monitor and rollback if p95 regresses >25% on prod slices (I'll be on call) :eyes:

sasha: acked. i'll put the dashboard link in the thread when ready.

liam: starting canaries now. ping me if you want to watch the trace stream. :rocket:
